From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC performance SLO items (post-call)

Hi John —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Summary + immediate next steps from our side below so we have alignment before we schedule a joint perf run with your network team.

Quick summary of what we heard:
- Target SLO: P95 latency <= 150ms for typical requests (~256 tokens).
- Steady-state concurrency: ~80 requests/sec; expected spikes up to ~300 for short windows.
- Streaming: yes — client requires partial-token streaming (progressive flush) with end-to-end latency budget for first partial chunk <= 100ms.
- Deployment: Private/VPC deployment in your us-east-1 account, connecting via Transit Gateway today.

Open items we need from you to size the test and validate the network path:
1) Confirm the specific steady and burst concurrency numbers you want us to validate (80 steady / 300 burst OK to proceed?).
2) Provide a network diagram (VPCs, TGW attachments, customer NAT/egress path) and a contact on the network team we can loop in for iperf/traceroute tests.
3) Confirm whether TLS is terminated at a customer LB or if mutual TLS will be used end-to-end to the inference hosts.
4) Any firewall rules / IP allowlists required for our perf runner to reach the inference endpoint (we can provide IP ranges and ports).

Proposed next step from Redwood: schedule a 30–60 minute joint test window where we run a perf profile that includes steady-state 80 concurrency and two short burst tests to 300 concurrency, plus streaming tests that measure P95 for initial token flush. We will bring a perf plan and bring limited trusted IPs to allow.

Attachments: I linked a brief test plan template and an example perf matrix for you to review before the run. Please attach your network diagram if you have one and point us to the right network contact.

If that all sounds good I can propose two times tomorrow: 09:00 PT or 11:00 PT.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — confirming details from our side:
- SLO: P95 <= 150ms for 256-token typical payloads.
- Concurrency: steady ~80 QPS, planned production bursts to ~300 QPS for up to 90s.
- Streaming: yes, client expects partial results with first-chunk latency <100ms; overall end-to-end budget for interactive flows is 200ms.

Network notes:
- We currently connect via AWS Transit Gateway in us-east-1. Egress to the internet goes through a managed NAT gateway in a central account.
- We do have VPC peering between our app VPCs and the inference VPCs for some regions, but for the deployment you propose we'll use TGW attachments.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to the inference endpoint; we will add allowlist entries for your test IPs once you provide them.

I've attached our network diagram (acme-network-diagram.pdf) and looped in Alex (network ops). Alex will coordinate the iperf/traceroute windows.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC performance SLO items (post-call)

Awesome — thanks for the diagram and the confirmation. A few technical clarifications and the perf plan we'll run on Thu 04 Mar at 09:00 PT (we'll send calendar invite):

Network / infra clarifications:
- For lowest jitter and consistent P95, we recommend either direct VPC peering or Transit Gateway with ENI attachments in the same AZs as your app fleet to avoid cross-AZ hops. TGW is fine if ENI locality is preserved.
- Internal latency budget: to hit a ~150ms P95 for 256-token requests with streaming, we need the app->inference RTT (L4/L7) to be <10ms median and <25ms 95th between your app and the inference ENIs. Can you confirm whether that is achievable with your current VPC layout?
- MTU / Path MTU: please confirm you don't have path MTU <1400 on any hops — small MTU causing fragmentation can add variability to streaming performance.
- TLS: mutual TLS endpoints are preferred for enterprise deployments; if you plan to terminate TLS at a customer LB, we need the LB to preserve client source IPs for accurate capacity planning.

Perf run (what we will execute):
1) Baseline: 15 minutes at 80 QPS (sustained) — measure P50/P95/P99 for initial token flush + end-to-end.
2) Burst tests: 3 x 60s bursts to 300 QPS spaced across the run to validate autoscaling and tail behavior.
3) Streaming: repeated interactive flows that measure first-chunk latency and partial flush behavior. We'll instrument both client-side and server-side traces for correlation.
4) Network tests: coordinated iperf3 runs (UDP + TCP), traceroute, and a small HTTP payroll to verify TLS handshakes and keepalive behavior.

Pre-test items from Acme: a) allowlist our test IPs (we will send these), b) provide a target endpoint (DNS) and an ingress port, c) confirm contact for the iperf window (Alex).

Attachments: redwood_perf_test_plan.pdf (detailed steps), acme_perf_requirements.xlsx (template for you to fill).

If you can confirm the internal latency budget and the allowlist steps we'll lock the run.

Thanks —
Marissa
